subject: n_paraffin_decay_ratio
magnitude: w(nC n+1)/w(nC n) = 0.88 default for n > 20
conditions: use when no measured n-alkane distribution; not valid below n-C20
citation: Ameri Mahabadian, Chapoy, Burgass, Tohidi (Heriot-Watt), citing Coutinho and Daridon 2001 and Ji 2004
notes: Exponential decay of n-paraffins above C20 is the standard assumption.

subject: n_paraffin_decay_ratio
magnitude: model oils with decay ratio 0.88 (fast) and 0.92 (slow); 0.9 separates small and large decay
conditions: simulated oils: 15 wt% total wax, Mw 230, C15 solvent, heaviest n-alkane C50 or C90
citation: Coutinho, J.A.P., Daridon, J.L. (2005). The limitations of the cloud point measurement techniques and the influence of the oil composition on its detection. Petroleum Science and Technology, 23, 1113-1128.
notes: Values chosen to bracket real crudes. Cutting paraffins above C50 (sampling loss) is Oil E: 15 to 13.77 wt% wax.

subject: n_paraffin_distribution_shape
magnitude: rising ratio 1.03 from C20 to C26, decay ratio 0.80 above C26; significant n-alkanes up to C48 (extrapolated below 0.01 wt%)
conditions: Java (Indonesia) Crude A, 41.4 API, conventional GC to C38, nC20+ GC 15.60 wt% normalised to wax content 14.08 wt%
citation: Kurniawan, M., Adiwar, Mulia, K., Anwar, C. (2013). Wax precipitation in crude oil by Coutinho model based on conventional gas chromatography data. Scientific Contributions Oil & Gas, 36(2), 75-82.
notes: Distribution peaks near C26 in wt%. Mass-weighted mean carbon number of the normalised C20-C48 table is about 26.

subject: wax_content_method
magnitude: direct precipitation wax / DSC C20+ = median 3.1 (range 1.8 to 13) over 19 crudes; HTGC C20+ minus DSC C20+ mean -0.1 wt%, mean absolute 1.3 wt%
conditions: crudes 10.7-45 API from North Sea, Africa, Middle East, Asia, Mediterranean, South America; DSC on raw crude, HTGC n-paraffin C20+, solvent precipitation
citation: Robustillo, M.D., Martos, C., Espada, J.J., Coto, B. (2012). Assessment of different methods to determine the total wax content of crude oils. Energy & Fuels, 26, 6352-6357.
notes: Precipitated solid traps oil; after porosity correction NMR and DSC agree. So a UOP 46 style wax number is NOT the n-paraffin amount the thermo engine needs: divide by roughly 2 to 4.

subject: multisolid_model
magnitude: experimental minus calculated cloud point -4.15 to +3.95 K, AAD 2.1 K, bias -0.1 K
conditions: 8 North Sea dead oils of Pedersen et al. 1991 (oils 1, 2, 5, 8, 10, 11, 12, 15); PR EOS liquid, pure solids, gamma C7+ split
citation: Lira-Galeana, C., Firoozabadi, A., Prausnitz, J.M. (1996). Thermodynamics of wax precipitation in petroleum mixtures. AIChE Journal (LBL-36816 preprint).
notes: Rows in validation_sets.csv.

subject: WAT_minus_pour_point
magnitude: microscopy WPT minus pour point (ASTM D5853) = 29.3 C mean (25.8 to 34.0)
conditions: 13 Colombian wellhead crudes, 37-43 API, from one main reservoir (Escobar and Pelaez 2000 data)
citation: Escobar-Remolina, J.C.M., Barrios-Ortiz, W., Santoyo-Ramirez, G. (2009). CT&F 3(5), 35-51.
notes: WPT 51-55.6 C at only modest wax. Live or dead state of the WPT measurement is unclear.

subject: modified_multisolid
magnitude: calc minus exp WPT +1.6 C mean, MAE 1.9 C (max +6.0 C)
conditions: 13 Colombian crudes, tuned multisolid model
citation: Escobar-Remolina et al. 2009

subject: solid_phase_model
magnitude: Won regular solution +0.15 to +0.83 K; Pedersen ideal solid solution +5.2 to +5.9 K vs measured
conditions: Dauphin et al. 1999 synthetic waxes: n-C10 (80 mol%) + C18-C36 exponential, with and without C25-C29 gap; PR EOS liquid
citation: Bhangale, A.Y. (2007). Modeling of wax precipitation. MS thesis, University of Alaska Fairbanks.
notes: Ideal solid solution over-predicts WAT, as in this study.

subject: distribution_gap
magnitude: removing C26-C28 or C25-C29 from an exponential C18-C36 wax raised measured WAT by 0.9 and 1.6 K
conditions: Dauphin systems A, B, C (C10 solvent, about 20 mol% wax), mole fractions renormalised so heavier ones increase
citation: Dauphin et al. 1999 data as tabulated by Bhangale 2007
notes: Heaviest n-alkanes control WAT; gaps change mole fractions of the heavy end.

subject: predictive_UNIQUAC
magnitude: Erickson oil 6 +11 C; Hammami-Raines A-1 -3 C (vs CPM); A-10 +1.7 C; Daridon oil B within data uncertainty about 2 K
conditions: limited n-paraffin data extrapolated exponentially (Erickson oil 6 from C30 to C55)
citation: Coutinho, J.A.P., Edmonds, B., Moorwood, T., Szczepanski, R., Zhang, X. (2006). Reliable wax predictions for flow assurance. Energy & Fuels.
notes: Large errors arise when the heavy n-paraffin tail is extrapolated, not measured.

subject: model_family
magnitude: AD% PC-SAFT 2.3-5.5, Lira-Galeana multisolid 11.5-16.8, Ji solid solution 19.2-25.3
conditions: one studied crude (aromaticity 0.98), probably live oil at several pressures
citation: Petroleum Science 2015 paper (s12182-015-0071-4), title not read
notes: Percentages look very large for K; check definition before use.

subject: multisolid_ideal_liquid
magnitude: pure-solid multisolid with ideal liquid and Coutinho properties under-predicts WAT by 4.7 to 5.0 K (Dauphin), 5.4 K (Java crude), 3 to 9 K (quaternary WDT)
conditions: this study, test_thermo.py T3-T5
citation: This study (agents/thermo/test_output.txt)
notes: Model-derived, not a literature fact.

subject: ideal_solid_solution
magnitude: ideal solid solution with Coutinho properties over-predicts WAT by +5.5 to +6.8 K (Dauphin), +6.3 K (Java crude, M 162.9)
conditions: this study, test_thermo.py
citation: This study
notes: Model-derived.

subject: coutinho_total_enthalpy_ideal
magnitude: ideal pure-solid solubility with Coutinho Tm and total enthalpy over-predicts saturation T of nC38 and nC50 in heptane by 3.9 to 7.2 C
conditions: Zhou et al. 2026 DSC solubility data, 0.7-5.7 mol%
citation: This study vs Zhou et al. (2026) Processes 14, 1207
notes: Zhou's own DSC crystallisation enthalpies (C38 96.6+7.8 kJ, C50 142.3 kJ) are lower than Coutinho eq 3 (131 and 176 kJ); with them the ideal model fits within about 0.3 mol%.

subject: wax_content
magnitude: +4 to +8 C per doubling of n-paraffin content (multisolid: 2,5,10,20 wt% -> 14.3, 21.3, 25.8, 29.9 C; ideal SS 24.5, 33.0, 38.8, 44.4 C)
conditions: engine, gamma distribution mean C25, sd 5, oil M 220 g/mol, Coutinho properties
citation: This study (thermo_wat.py)
notes: Model-derived logarithmic dependence: WAT ~ a + b ln(wax).

subject: mean_carbon_number
magnitude: about +1.5 C (multisolid) to +1.7 C (ideal SS) per unit mean carbon number between C22 and C34 at 10 wt%
conditions: engine, sd 5, M 220
citation: This study (thermo_wat.py)
notes: Model-derived with tail cutoff 0.01 wt%.

subject: n_paraffin_tail_cutoff
magnitude: keeping n-paraffin traces down to 1e-4 instead of 0.01 wt% raises predicted WAT by about 6 C (bracket 36.5 to 42.7 C); 0.05 wt% cutoff lowers it to 32.1 C
conditions: engine, Java Crude A summary (14.08 wt%, mean C26.2, sd 4.8, gamma, M 162.9)
citation: This study (thermo_wat.py, test T9)
notes: Heaviest traces set the first crystal. Default 0.01 wt% follows Kurniawan 2013 extrapolation stop rule; with it the builder gives 36.5 C vs DSC 38 C.

subject: C20plus_content
magnitude: DSC-based C20+ 1.0 to 20.3 wt% over 32 crudes of 10.7-45 API, pour -38 to 39 C
conditions: Tables 4-5
citation: Robustillo et al. 2012 Energy & Fuels 26, 6352
notes: Use with model robustillo2012_C20plus to give the engine an n-paraffin amount from API and pour point.

subject: non_paraffinic_wax_formers
magnitude: fusion temperature of non-paraffinic part = n-alkane of same carbon number minus 70 K
conditions: Ji 2004 Heriot-Watt wax model
citation: Ji et al. 2004, quoted by Ameri Mahabadian et al.

subject: nC50_in_heptane_solubility
magnitude: nC50 in n-heptane: 0.73 mol% saturates at 57.52 C, 1.99 at 64.06 C, 3.41 at 68.16 C; nC38: 1.26 mol% at 40.22 C, 5.69 at 53.09 C
conditions: DSC precipitation on cooling
citation: Zhou, J., Pan, Z., Zhang, Y., Wu, H., Wu, G., Liu, J. (2026). Determination of solubilities of n-alkanes (nC38-nC50) in n-heptane, n-nonane and n-dodecane using the DSC method. Processes, 14, 1207.
notes: Test data for the engine; paper's ideal-solution calc reproduced exactly for nC50 (0.74 vs 0.73, 2.01 vs 2.00, 3.69 vs 3.68 mol%).

subject: n_paraffin_correlations
magnitude: correlations for n-alkane content and distribution of waxy crudes proposed from detailed compositions of about 30 crudes
conditions: abstract only; equations not read
citation: Coutinho, J.A.P., Daridon, J.L. (2001). Low-pressure modeling of wax formation in crude oils. Energy & Fuels, 15, 1454-1460.
notes: Best unopened source: would give the n-paraffin amount and decay from bulk data.

subject: waxy_crude_cloud_point
magnitude: most measured cloud points of waxy crudes around 315 K
conditions: statement in text
citation: Coutinho and Daridon 2005, Pet Sci Technol 23, 1113
notes: Qualitative.
